report.summary: Transfer errors and slow requests coincide with an idle-in-transaction session blocking ledger_app sessions at 17:17:26-17:17:52. The outbox, consumer and pool are healthy. No request-level link to the 500s was observed.

findings.claim: A session idle in transaction blocked ledger_app sessions for up to ~2 s between 17:17:26 and 17:17:52.
findings.reason: Blocked sessions 75229 and 75230 waited on session 76388 (idle in transaction); a third waited on 75229, so the waits chained.

findings.claim: Transfers show 26 HTTP 500s (6.2%) and p95 1.43 s / p99 3.25 s, so the symptom is real.
findings.reason: The metrics are complete and show both server errors and a long latency tail.

findings.claim: The lock waits likely caused the slow and failed transfers. The outbox arrival dip (17-21 per 10 s in early buckets) matches the blocking window.
findings.reason: Arrivals fell from 28 to 17-21 per 10 s early in the window, matching the blocking period, then recovered to 28.

findings.claim: Outbox delivery, the consumer and the connection pool are not the cause.
findings.reason: All 394 deliveries succeeded at ~71 ms, nothing failed, there were 0 pool timeouts and 0 pending borrowers, and arrivals equal publications.

limitations: Blocking is sampled every 2 s, and no request or trace data links the 26 500s to specific lock waits.
The identity and code path of the idle-in-transaction session 76388 (role 'other') are unknown, and the runtime revision is marked dirty.

alternatives.reason: Pool pending was 0, there were 0 acquisition timeouts, and active connections peaked at 3 of 10.
